title: Load-balancer health check points at a readiness endpoint that fails during a cache warm
source_note: Failure pattern (a load-balancer health check checks readiness of a slow-warming dependency rather than liveness, so healthy instances get pulled from rotation during a routine event and the survivors overload) follows datacenter load-balancing guidance in the Google SRE Book. All services, change ids, paths, log lines, metrics, and timestamps are fabricated for evaluation.
incident_report: Since ~03:03 UTC the app is throwing 503s for most users. The load balancer shows most instances as unhealthy, but the instances themselves look fine. No application deploys. A load-balancer config change went in overnight.

signal_lines.msg: health check path updated to /ready (config change CR-9012)
scheduled nightly cache flush and rebuild started
18 of 24 app-server instances failing health check /ready (503 while the cache rebuilds)
only 6 instances in rotation; each at 95% CPU; 503 rate climbing
instances are healthy; /ready returns 503 only until the cache is warm (~10 min)
health check reverted to /healthz (liveness only); all instances back in rotation

ground_truth.root_cause: A config change (CR-9012) pointed the load balancer's health check at /ready, which returns 503 until a background cache is warm. When the nightly cache flush and rebuild ran, 18 of 24 app-server instances failed that health check - even though they could serve traffic - and the load balancer removed them from rotation. The remaining 6 instances overloaded (95% CPU) and started returning 503s. The instances were never unhealthy; the health check was testing readiness of a warming cache, not liveness. Recovery required reverting the health check to a liveness-only path.
evidence_path: app-lb INFO at 03:00: health check path changed to /ready (config change CR-9012)
the nightly cache flush and rebuild starts at 03:02
app-lb WARN: 18 of 24 instances fail /ready with 503 while the cache rebuilds
lb_healthy_instances drops from 24 to 6; the survivors overload and 5xx rate climbs to ~55%
app-server confirms the instances are healthy - /ready just returns 503 until the cache warms
recovery after the health check is reverted to /healthz (liveness only)
ground_truth.fix: Revert the health check to a liveness-only path (done). Separate liveness from readiness in the load-balancer config, make readiness failures reduce an instance's weight rather than remove it entirely, and never gate rotation on a slow-warming dependency.
